sources.title: PEARL
sources.text: About PEARL The Positive Emotion and Anxiety Research Laboratory (PEARL) specializes in discovering evidence-based solutions to reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression and increase life satisfaction and well-being. More about the Lab Take part in our studies Our current studies are evaluating the effects of a behavioral treatment on positive and negative emotions, behaviors, and brain systems that are important for our overall well-being. We are also evaluating the effects of cannabidiol (CBD) on the biological and stress responses underlying anxiety disorders. Learn More Our Research Publications Previous Studies Open Positions We are not currently recruiting.

sources.title: About Us
sources.text: About PEARL Our Vision The Positive Emotion and Anxiety Research Laboratory specializes in discovering evidence-based solutions to reduce symptoms of anxiety and depression and increase life satisfaction and well-being. Our Mission To enhance our understanding of the factors that cause and maintain anxiety and depression so that more effective, efficient, personalized, and widely accessible treatments can be developed. Our mission extends beyond the alleviation of distress and negative emotions - but also endeavors to boost positive emotions, social relationship functioning, life satisfaction, and well-being. We seek to achieve these aims by bringing together insights and experimental approaches across multiple areas of psychology, including affective neuroscience, social psychology, cognitive psychology, and clinical psychology. sources.text: Meet Our Team Principal Investigator Charlie Taylor, Ph.D. Dr. Taylor is an Associate Professor of Psychiatry at UC San Diego and the Director of the Positive Emotion & Anxiety Research Laboratory (PEARL). He received his B.Sc. in Psychology at McMaster University (Hamilton, ON, Canada) and Ph.D. in Clinical Psychology from the University of British Columbia (Vancouver, BC, Canada). He has over 15 years of experience specializing in the assessment and treatment of anxiety and depression. Dr. Taylor directs an active program of clinical research funded by the National Institute of Mental Health and Brain and Behavior Foundation. Members Doctoral Students Madeleine Rassaby Hi there! My name is Madeleine, and I am a 5th-year doctoral candidate at the San Diego State University/University of California, San Diego Joint Doctoral Program in Clinical Psychology working under the mentorship of Dr. Charles Taylor and Dr. Murray Stein. My research interests focus on optimizing evidence-based treatments for anxiety, depressive, and trauma-related disorders with the goals of reducing symptom severity and promoting positive emotional and social functioning. Outside of my research and clinical work, I love spending time with my family and friends, being active outdoors or at the gym, cooking, traveling, and admiring San Diego's beautiful beaches. Isabella Spaulding Hello! My name is Isabella and I’m a first year doctoral student in the SDSU/UC San Diego Joint Doctoral Program in Clinical Psychology. Before joining PEARL I completed my B.S. in Clinical Psychology at Tufts University and then worked as a postbaccalaureate fellow in the Section on Development and Affective Neuroscience at the National Institute of Mental Health. My research interests are focused on exploring the cognitive and neurobiological mechanisms underlying mood, anxiety, and trauma disorders, and how these insights might inform the development of novel treatments. I’m also particularly interested in better understanding the impacts (e.g., biological, social) of early adversity on individuals with psychological disorders in adulthood, in an effort to identify potential treatment targets and ultimately improve outcomes for this population. Outside of the lab I love to spend time at the beach, try new recipes, and travel! Research Coordinators Marissa Larkin Hello! My name is Marissa, and I am a lab coordinator at PEARL. I graduated from the University of Utah in 2023 with a B.S. in Psychology and a minor in Applied Positive Psychology. During my undergraduate career, I worked in the Child Adaptation and Neurodevelopment Lab as a research assistant and wrote an honors thesis focusing on emotion dysregulation and trauma history. Soon after graduation, I joined PEARL! I work mainly with the CBD study, but also assist with all other areas of work within the lab. I plan to attend graduate school for clinical psychology and work as a practicing clinician long-term. My research interests broadly surround anxiety and depression intervention. In my free time, I enjoy going to the beach, on a hike, or to concerts. Juliana Himawan Hi! I’m Juliana, and I graduated from UC San Diego in December 2024 with a B.S. in Cognitive Behavioral Neuroscience and a minor in General Biology. I’ve been a part of the PEARL team since 2022, and I wrote my senior thesis titled, "Elevated Anxiety is Associated with Greater Activation in the Striatum in a Transdiagnostic Sample." Currently, I work as a coordinator, focusing primarily on our anxiety and depression study. Outside of lab, I enjoy practicing yoga, baking sourdough, and spending time at the beach. Clinical Research Assistants Giovanni Rodriguez Hello! My name is Gio and I recently graduated from UCSD with a B.S in Cognitive & Behavioral Neuroscience major and a minor in Biology. I joined PEARL in April 2025 to gain more hands-on research within the field of clinical psychology and to deepen my knowledge of stress and anxiety disorders . In the lab, I am currently responsible for phone screening and assisting with brain imaging . When I'm not in the lab, some things I enjoy doing are exercising, playing tennis, watching movies, and reading . In the future, I hope to pursue higher education and achieve my goal of becoming a neuroscientist to help research substance abuse and mood disorders. Maxon Jin Hello everyone! My name is Maxon, and I’m a fourth-year student at UCSD majoring in clinical psychology. I joined PEARL in April of 2025 because I wanted to gain experience and develop skills relevant to working with a clinical population as I work towards a career in psychotherapy. In the lab, I am currently the head of phone screening, an intake scheduler, and a trained confederate. Outside of the lab, I like to hang out with my friends, listen to music, play the guitar, play all kinds of sports, and do photography. In the future, I hope to pursue a PsyD and become a licensed therapist specializing in depression and anxiety disorders. Zainab Subhi Hi! My name is Zainab, and I’m a fourth-year student at UCSD studying Human Health Psychology and Biology. As a research assistant, my responsibilities include serving as a confederate and assisting with brain imaging, data entry, phone screenings, and fidelity ratings. What I value most about PEARL is our innovative approach to exploring treatments that go beyond what is currently considered the standard. Outside of the lab, I enjoy cooking, traveling, and exploring new makeup and skincare trends. I hope to attend medical school and become a physician dedicated to advancing PEARL’s mission of improving treatments and patient care. Orli Gollan-Myers Hi! My name is Orli and I’m a 4th year at UCSD. My major is Psychology, and I joined PEARL in October of 2025. I became a part of PEARL because I am very passionate about those who struggle with anxiety, depression, and other mental illnesses, and I want to contribute to helping them. In the lab, I’m currently responsible for being a confederate. Outside of the lab, I like to dance, play instruments, lift weights, and go to cafes with my friends. In the future, I hope to get a Ph.D in clinical psychology!! Soha Shariff Hii everyone! My name is Soha . I’m a 2nd year Neurobiology major at UCSD. I joined PEARL in March 2026 to gain more hands-on experience working in a research lab, specifically gaining that one-on-one experience with participants that you typically don't get in many labs. In the lab, I am currently working as a confederate and will also soon become a phone screener. Outside of the lab, I like to bake, watch movies, and go to the beach with my family and friends. In the future, I hope to pursue medical school and find a career I can pursue for the rest of myself. In addition, I am hoping to become more fluent in Urdu, I would love to travel to different countries around the world to understand different medical processes and gaps they may have. Nathan Su Hello! My name is Nathan and I am a fourth year student at UCSD pursuing my B.S. in Clinical Psychology. I joined PEARL in March of 2026. The reason I joined was because of the 5 core values they place a big emphasis on, which align with my values, and their research on Anxiety and Mood disorders and new treatment methods for them. In the lab, I work as a phone screener where I conduct initial phone screenings with potential research participants, documenting and assessing eligibility for our PRAM study enrollment. Outside of the lab I am a jack of many trades. I enjoy reading (mainly self-help books), skateboarding, dirt biking, basketball, snowboarding, working out, going to the beach, thrifting, and trying new things. In the future, I plan to pursue either a Masters degree in Marriage and Family Therapy or a PsyD in Counseling Psychology. Kalpita Nath Hello ! My name is Kalpita . I’m a fourth year at UCSD, and I am majoring in Clinical Psychology and Cognitive & Behavioural Neuroscience . I joined PEARL in March of 2026 . I became a part of PEARL because I wanted to learn about research in therapy intervention development and I found so much value in the emphasis they place on improving positive emotions . In the lab, I am currently involved in confederate interactions and brain imaging . Outside of the lab, I like to do oil paintings, doodle , cook, and watch some good TV shows. In the future, I hope to pursue a PhD in Clinical psychology and go along the lines of neuropsychology, so that I can continue working on developing behavioural interventions for those with neurological conditions. Navadeep Manam Hi! My name is Navadeep, and I’m currently a third year student at UCSD studying human biology. I’ve always been fascinated by the role of mental health within patient care, which led me to join PEARL in April of 2026. I wanted to contribute to research focusing on treating anxiety and depression while also getting to experience the research environment in a professional setting. In the lab, I work as a phone screener, where I interview potential participants to assess eligibility for the study. Outside of the lab, I love watching movies, reading books, playing chess, and playing video games. In the future, I hope to go to medical school. I am particularly interested in addressing the gap between clinical patient care and mental health support, ensuring that psychological well-being is as fundamental a priority within the medical field as anything else. Ruby Orellana Hi everyone! My name is Ruby , and I’m a rising third year at the University of California San Diego majoring in clinical psychology. I joined PEARL in April 2026 to gain valuable research experience and learn more about depression, anxiety, and how these disorders are being studied and treated in the lab. I’ve always been interested in mental health, so I’m excited to continue learning more about clinical psychology through research and collaboration with others in the lab. Outside of the lab, I enjoy playing volleyball, grabbing dinner with friends, and reading books in my free time. In the future, I hope to earn my PsyD and pursue a career in clinical psychology. A fun fact about me is that I have a twin sister! Denise Ramirez Hi everyone! My name is Denise and I’m an upcoming fourth year psychology student at University of California, San Diego. I joined PEARL in May of 2026 with hopes of deepening my research skills and contributing to research that is both innovative and meaningful to me. I really admire the values at PEARL, especially the work being done to better treat individuals impacted by depression and anxiety. In the lab, I am involved in confederate interactions and phone screening, but am hoping to contribute to different areas in PEARL! Outside of the lab, I love going to the beach, travelling, going on hikes, eating good food, and spending time with my friends and family. In the future, I plan on pursuing a graduate degree in maybe therapy/counseling, but am still deciding what exact path I want to take! In addition to having a career that I am passionate about, in the future, I hope to travel the world and continue learning new things. Pets Bruiser One of Charlie's two dogs. Fern One of Charlie's two dogs. Jerry and Harry These are Bella's two dogs. Jerry is a 1-year-old Brindle Boerboel, and Harry is a 6-month-old Rottweiler & Caucasian Shepherd mix. They love to play fight with each other. Jerry is about 150 lbs, and Harry is about 100! Athena Athena is Rayya's 3-year-old rescue cat and is super friendly to everyone she meets. She craves everything chicken-related and makes biscuits on your neck until eternity. She loves neck scratches, but definitely will let you know when you are overstepping her boundaries. In her free time, she likes licking plastic to annoy her mom. Jackson, Molly, and Poppins Meet Lora's kitties: Jackson, Molly, and Poppins! This black-and-white trio fills the house with love and just enough chaos. Together, they're a goofy, cuddly, and perpetually hungry bunch... and most importantly, absolute sweethearts <3 Molo This is Molo! Molo is a part of Denise’s family and is a bernedoodle originally born in Utah. Molo loves to eat Filipino food, lay down, and play with his toy cow. Molo is just as tall as Denise when he stands up and loves belly rubs. The Altman Clinical and Translational Research Institute is the building immediately down the street from the Campus Point Patient & Visitor Parking Structure. It is across the street from the emergency entrance of the Gary and Mary West Emergency Department. Public Transportation Options Take the Blue Line trolley to the UCSD Health La Jolla station.
